html:
An English buccaneer, explorer and naturalist who was the first Englishman to explore parts of Australia and the first person to sail around the world three times.

Dampier spent his youth at sea and among the pirates of the Caribbean and the Pacific coast of Spanish America. In 1688, on the buccaneer ship Cygnet, he landed on the northwest coast of Australia. His book A New Voyage Round the World (1697) was a bestseller, full of careful notes on winds, plants, animals and peoples. It won him command of a navy ship, the Roebuck, which reached Shark Bay in Western Australia in 1699. There he collected plants that still survive in Oxford. He wrote harshly of the Aboriginal people he met, a view that lasted in Britain for a long time.

He was a poor commander, and the Roebuck sank on the way home. On a later privateering voyage his ship picked up Alexander Selkirk, the castaway whose story fed Robinson Crusoe. His books influenced Gulliver's Travels and later naturalists. He bridges the age of Francis Drake and that of James Cook.
